# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👉 ✊ ✌ 🤳 🖐 🤜 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤳 🖐 🤜 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤳 👎 👉 ✊ ✌ 🤳 🤜 ✌ ☝ 🤳 🤜 ✌ ☝]

I can see a blue light, display reading 0, and three wires in order red, green, blue. The bomb is embossed “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” so Blind should not cut a wire unless Mute’s manual gives an overriding instruction. I cannot yet decode Mute’s gesture sequence.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT blue. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind: do not cut any wire unless the manual explicitly requires it.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The new single gesture has no established meaning to me, and Blind cannot see it. The visible warning remains clear: no wire should be cut absent an explicit manual instruction. I will tell Mute that I need a decodable gesture convention or a direct indication of the required physical action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gestures but we have no shared gesture code, so I cannot decode them. Please indicate the manual's required physical action with an established/simple convention or send a repeatable code legend. Current bomb remains: blue light, display 0, wires red-green-blue, and embossed warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change. Keep clear of all three wires; the bomb explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. We are awaiting Mute's manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤏 👎]

Mute’s long gesture begins with the first 26 gesture symbols in the published order, which appears to establish an alphabetic code. The remaining symbols decode approximately as “CUT GREEN B…”, but the final instruction is incomplete or ambiguous. The earlier gesture sequence appears to encode color words, including BLUE, GREEN, and RED. Because the visible bomb explicitly says not to cut any wire, Blind should wait for the complete manual instruction rather than act on an incomplete phrase.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I infer your codebook is the first 26 gesture symbols in listed order, followed by a message approximately CUT GREEN B. Please send the complete final word/instruction; I will not tell Blind to cut based on an incomplete phrase, especially because the bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest encoded message appears to begin CUT GREEN B, but it is incomplete/ambiguous. Do not cut anything yet: the bomb visibly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and I am requesting clarification.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤏 👋 👆 🫸 ✌ 🤏 🤜 👋 🫳]

The gesture alphabet is now clear: its first 26 symbols map to A–Z in the published order, with 🤏 used as a word separator. Mute’s message decodes as “CUT GREEN WIRE TO”, so it is still incomplete: it must specify a destination or position before Blind acts. I will request the continuation and tell Blind not to act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded: CUT GREEN WIRE TO. Please send the remaining destination/position immediately. I understand 🤏 as the word separator.")
speak(to="blind", text="Manual instruction decoded so far: CUT GREEN WIRE TO ... The required destination is missing. Do not cut or move a wire until the instruction is complete.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤏 🤜 👋 🫳]

The complete Turn 4 message decodes as “CUT GREEN WIRE TWO.” Mute’s new message repeats the ending, “E TWO,” confirming that the target is wire two. Since wire 2 is green, the manual’s instruction is to cut the green second wire; it overrides the printed warning for this bomb configuration.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Complete manual instruction decoded and confirmed: CUT GREEN WIRE TWO. Cut wire 2, the green wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded complete instruction as CUT GREEN WIRE TWO; I have told Blind to cut wire 2, green.")
```
